shared_elements: rows of repeated small vertical strokes/signs
figural carving on a rock surface
justification: The only real correspondence is that both surfaces carry rows of repeated small vertical marks — glyph columns and figures densely filling a stela in A, versus crew-stroke ship outlines stacked in a loose vertical sequence in B — a coincidence of repetition rather than of motif. A depicts elaborate anthropomorphic figures with headdresses and blocky script arranged in framed registers filling the whole field, while B depicts only stripped-down linear boats with upturned prows floating on an otherwise empty rock face; the drawing conventions (dense modelled relief vs bare single-line contour) share nothing.
